question_text: According to the course material, ENT 207 Basic Financial Literacy is a semester course work of two credit units available to all students in:
option_a: the Department of Entrepreneurial Studies, Faculty of Management
explanation: It will be available to all students in the Department of Entrepreneurial Studies, Faculty of Management.

question_text: According to the course material, the course consists of 4 modules involving the subject area of Basic Financial Literacy, with 18 study units.
option_a: True: 4 modules and 18 units are listed
option_b: False: it has 14 GST culture units
explanation: There are 18 units in 4 modules.

question_text: According to the course material, in general terms investment involves:
option_a: spending of money with the hope of reaping some financial benefits
explanation: Investment involves spending of money with the hope of reaping some financial benefits.

question_text: According to economists as cited in the course material, investment is regarded as savings embarked upon as a result of:
option_a: delayed consumption
explanation: Economists regard investment as savings embarked upon as a result of delayed consumption.

question_text: According to the course material, in finance an investment involves utilization of funds in acquisition of financial assets such as stocks, bonds, bullion, real properties, and precious items.
option_a: True: those assets are listed
option_b: False: only GST textbooks are assets
option_c: False: only culture-area maps are assets
option_d: False: only Portuguese caravels are assets
explanation: Finance: utilization of funds in acquisition of stocks, bonds, bullion, real properties, and precious items.

question_text: According to Beattie (2017) as cited in the course material, three basic groups of investments are:
option_a: ownership investment, lending investment, and cash investment
explanation: Beattie identifies ownership, lending, and cash investment.

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 1 also lists types of investment as Ownership Investment, Lending Investment, and:
option_a: Marketable Security Investment
explanation: Types: Ownership, Lending, and Marketable Security Investment.

question_text: According to the course material, the fundamental purpose of investment is to generate earnings, which for financial products can come as interest, capital gain over the principal, and:
option_a: dividend from stock
explanation: Earnings can come as interest, capital gain and dividend from stock.

question_text: According to the course material, Earnings = Prevailing Price of Stock less Original price, and capital gain is measured by the disparity between original price and:
option_a: current market of the product
explanation: Capital gain is the disparity between original price and current market of the product.

question_text: According to the course material, the essence of investment hinges on expected returns, which may be in form of capital gain or investment income that include dividends, interest, and rental income, among others.
option_a: True: those return forms are listed
option_c: False: only amalgamation surplus is a return
option_d: False: only Ofo justice is a return
explanation: Expected returns include capital gain or investment income (dividends, interest, rental income).

question_text: According to the Cambridge Dictionary (2017) as cited, venture creation refers to the process of converting a new idea or technology into a business undertaking which can succeed and is invariably capable of:
option_a: attracting investors
explanation: Capable of attracting investors.

question_text: According to Swier (2007) as cited, venture creation refers to an action initiated for starting business venture with the intent of filling the gap between an initiative and a:
option_a: capitalized business
explanation: Filling the gap between an initiative and a capitalized business.

question_text: According to the course material, most venture capitalists will only be interested in investing in a venture that portrays great fundamentals such as competent management, profitable market, novel product, and:
option_a: reasonable quantum of sales revenue or turnover
explanation: Fundamentals include competent management, profitable market, novel product, and reasonable sales revenue.

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 2 objectives include explaining venture creation, identifying stages in the process of venture creation, and listing responsibilities of entrepreneurs in venture creation.
option_a: True: those three objectives are listed
explanation: Unit 2 objectives cover meaning, process stages, and entrepreneur responsibilities.

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 3 treats diversification as a basis of investment portfolio, including meaning of diversification, using it in investment, advantages and disadvantages, and:
option_a: ways to avoid inappropriate diversification
explanation: Section 3.4: Ways to Avoid Inappropriate Diversification.

question_text: According to the course material, you cannot just hold stocks without monitoring the pulse of the capital market to take advantage of price fluctuations; that discussion is called:
option_a: value investment
explanation: Value investment is discussed because you cannot just hold stocks without monitoring the market.

question_text: According to the course material, a hedge is an investment undertaken in order to reduce the risk of adverse price movements in a financial asset, normally by taking:
option_a: an offsetting position in a related security, such as a futures contract
explanation: A hedge consists of taking an offsetting position in a related security, such as a futures contract.

question_text: According to the course material, in simple terms a hedge is used to reduce any substantial losses that may occur in investment which has to do with financial assets in the capital market.
option_a: True: that simple definition is given
explanation: A hedge is used to reduce substantial losses on capital-market financial assets.

question_text: According to the course material, it is advisable to engage services of brokerage firms (as traders in financial market) since they are professionals in such market.
option_a: True: stated in the hedging unit introduction
option_c: False: only the Alaafin may trade
explanation: Engage brokerage firms since they are professionals in such market.

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 4 also discusses advantages and disadvantages of using hedging to ensure investing profitably in the capital market.
option_a: True: sections 3.3.1 and 3.3.2
option_b: False: only culture-area advantages are listed
option_c: False: hedging has no disadvantages in the material
explanation: Advantages and disadvantages of hedging are discussed.

question_text: According to the course material, Module 1 provides the necessary background knowledge on investment.
option_a: True: stated after the unit list
explanation: Module 1 provides background knowledge on investment.

question_text: According to the course material, some elements of risk are inherent in any form of investment but risks vary from one investment to another, and the choice of investment is informed by the degree of risk involved, which can be ameliorated with:
option_a: a combination of investments
explanation: Risk can be ameliorated with a combination of investments.

question_text: According to the course material, an investment in good financial investment is fraught with reasonable level of market liquidity, and to assess the value of a financial investment a mechanism known as valuation becomes relevant.
option_a: True: liquidity and valuation are named
option_d: False: only the Alaafin values assets
explanation: Market liquidity and valuation are named.

option_a: True: listed on the title page
explanation: Course Writer: Dr. Sheu Abdullahi Araga (Department of Financial Studies, NOUN).
